readMe: Every public claim STANCH makes, with its status, the class of evidence behind it, where that evidence lives, and what it does not prove.
Status and evidence class are independent axes. Status is how much of the claim the evidence supports. Evidence class is what kind of observation produced it.
Partial evidence is described in the row and never raises its status.
A claim may not be promoted above UNMEASURED until the file named in evidence[] exists in this repository.
The negation belongs inside the claim sentence, not in a footnote.

statusDefinitions.SUPPORTED: The listed evidence supports the claim within its stated scope.
statusDefinitions.PARTIAL: The listed evidence supports only part of the claim; limitations identify the unsupported portion.
statusDefinitions.UNMEASURED: No observation or test currently supports the claim.
statusDefinitions.NOT_CLAIMED: The capability is explicitly outside the current submission claim set.

evidenceClassDefinitions.studio_next_observation: A time-bound read or interaction on Studio Next, chain 61997.
evidenceClassDefinitions.consensus_receipt: A finalized GenLayer transaction whose validators independently agreed on a non-deterministic result under an equivalence principle.
evidenceClassDefinitions.local_test: A deterministic result from the GenLayer testing suite against a local or simulated validator set. Not network evidence.
evidenceClassDefinitions.source_inspection: A property established by reading committed source, reproducible by a stated grep.
evidenceClassDefinitions.synthetic_fixture: A deterministic result produced from controlled fixture data.
evidenceClassDefinitions.publisher_claim: A statement or status returned by our own service or interface, about itself.

standingCaveats: All work runs on Studio Next with valueless test tokens. No amount recorded here is money.
Nothing here is an audit, a production-readiness claim, or a third-party endorsement.
STANCH is opt-in and pull-based. It cannot halt a contract that was not written to read it.
STANCH reads current state only. An exploit that has completed and left no readable trace cannot be halted.
A refusal observed through a read call is not a mined reverted transaction, and rows say which was observed.
Validator agreement on a classification is agreement, not correctness.
The demo target's defect was authored by us. Nothing here is detection of an unknown exploit in an unfamiliar contract.

A halt requires a transaction the network will process. On 2026-09-15 Studio Next stopped deciding non-deterministic transactions for a sustained period while deterministic writes continued normally; during that window no verdict could be reached and therefore no target could be halted. Removing the guardian's powers does not remove consensus availability as a failure mode.

claims.claim: A GenLayer Intelligent Contract on Studio Next can synchronously read another Intelligent Contract through gl.get_contract_at(addr).view(), both inside a write transaction and inside a view call.
limitations: The entire STANCH architecture depends on this single capability. If it fails, see PRD section 17, K1.
Upstream issue genvm-manager#20 reports synchronous reads are healthy on chain 4221, but exercised EOA-to-contract reads rather than contract-to-contract.

claims.claim: On Studio Next an asynchronous message emitted by an Intelligent Contract through gl.contract.get_at(addr).emit() does reach the callee, once the transaction carries a fee allocation for that message; the callee's counter went from 0 to 1 and recorded the emitting contract as its caller. This row records that observation and does not assert that STANCH depends on the behaviour either way.
limitations: Upstream issue genvm-manager#20 reports this path is broken on chain 4221 and was still open and unassigned as of 15 September 2026.
A pass on Studio Next does not mean the upstream defect is fixed on other networks.
STANCH chose the pull architecture regardless of this result. See DECISIONS.md D1.

claims.claim: On Studio Next, gl.contract.deploy called from inside a contract produces a contract that is reachable, though not immediately: the returned address read as 'contract not found' on the first attempt and answered about twenty seconds later, once the deploy message finalized.
limitations: The twenty-second figure is one polling observation on one deployment, not a measured latency bound.
A single read taken immediately after the parent transaction would have recorded this probe as a failure, and did on an earlier run. See DECISIONS.md D1.
STANCH does not use contract-initiated deployment. This row documents chain behaviour, not a STANCH capability.

claims.claim: On Studio Next, value paid into an Intelligent Contract arrives and value paid out through emit_transfer does not move, while the paying contract's own log records the payout as done; the balance was unchanged immediately after the call and again ninety seconds later.
claims.reproduce: See probes/PROBE.md, probe P4, and REPRODUCE.md section 2
limitations: One contract, one transfer, one amount. No sweep over amounts, recipients or message types was run.
Observed on Studio Next only. It does not establish the same behaviour on Asimov, Bradbury or any other GenLayer network.
It narrows rather than confirms upstream issue genvm-manager#20: on this chain internal emitted calls (P2) and contract-initiated deploys (P1) do execute, and only the value transfer does not.
No upstream maintainer has confirmed this reproduction at the time of writing.

claims.claim: STANCH cannot resume a halted target. No method sets a status back to RUNNING, and no code path writes RUNNING after construction; this is a property of the committed source, not a permission check that an operator could bypass.
limitations: Establishes the absence of a resume path in this version of the source, not across future versions.

A grep and five structural tests over committed source, plus one on-chain test that calls register and submit_claim against a halted key and observes the status stay HALTED. That test exercises the two public write methods; it does not enumerate every possible call sequence.
Not a VM-level capability proof and not a formal verification.
Does not prevent a target from ignoring a HALTED verdict; enforcement is the target's own guard clause.

claims.claim: STANCH has no write path to any contract it can halt. The symbols .emit(, emit_transfer, gl.deploy_contract and gl.evm.contract_interface appear nowhere in contracts/stanch.py.
limitations: A grep over committed source, not a VM-level capability proof.
Covers contracts/stanch.py only. The frontend and tests are separately scoped.
Does not establish that the GenVM would refuse such a write if it were added.

claims.claim: STANCH never takes custody of value. No payable method exists on the contract and its observed balance is zero.
claims.reproduce: grep -n 'payable' contracts/stanch.py && see REPRODUCE.md, balance read
limitations: Source inspection only. No balance read of the deployed STANCH address is recorded in this row, so the claim rests on the absence of a payable method rather than on an observed zero balance.
The ghost contract on the EVM layer is a separate surface and is not covered by this row.
Probe P4 shows that value which did reach a contract on this chain could not be paid out, so a balance arriving by some path not through a payable method would be stranded rather than recoverable.

claims.claim: A submitted claim whose pinned reading does not support the asserted pattern returns CLEAR and does not halt the target; the target was still RUNNING after the verdict.
limitations: One refused claim is one observation, not a measured false-positive rate.
The refusal was produced by the classifier under the standard fixed in code; a differently worded false claim may not be refused.
No adversarial sweep over claim phrasings has been run, and the injection attack in PRD section 20 could not be run at all: the Studio Next outage in DECISIONS.md D-010 blocked every further verdict.
The claim record and its pinned reading are readable on chain at the STANCH address in evidence/studio-next/deployment.json, so a reviewer can re-derive this row without trusting our transcript.

claims.claim: STANCH deployed with an empty upgraders list and four locked slots, read from inside the VM through gl.storage.Root.get(); no upgrade attempt was made against it, so the refusal half of this claim is unmeasured and the claim does not assert that an upgrade would fail.
limitations: The refusal half is UNMEASURED. Neither genlayer-py 0.19.0rc2 nor genlayer-js 2.0.0-rc.1 exposes a code upgrade path for Intelligent Contracts, so no upgrade transaction could be constructed to be refused.

No JSON-RPC method on Studio Next returns the root slot; gen_getContractState, sim_getContractState, gen_getUpgraders and gen_dbg_getContractState all return Method not found. The list is read by a view method on the contract itself.
That the contract reports its own upgraders list is a publisher_claim about our own code unless a reviewer reads the same slot independently.
Immutability of the standard is not immutability of the classifier; validator model behaviour is outside this claim.
Does not establish that the standard is correct, only that it is not writable through any method STANCH exposes.

claims.claim: A claim pointing at a genuinely violated invariant in CISTERN returned EXPLOIT under validator consensus and flipped the registered status to HALTED in a finalized transaction.
limitations: CISTERN's defect was authored by us for demonstration; this is not detection of an unknown exploit in an unfamiliar contract.
Validator agreement is agreement, not correctness.
One halt is one observation, not a measured detection rate.

claims.claim: After the status flip, a CISTERN state-changing call reverted with STANCH_HALTED, and the refusal was produced by CISTERN reading STANCH, not by STANCH writing to CISTERN.
limitations: Demonstrates enforcement in a target we wrote to cooperate. An uncooperative target is unprotected by design.
Records whether the refusal was a mined revert or a read-call failure; these are not the same evidence.

claims.claim: A claim whose reading was gathered successfully but contains no value capable of deciding the asserted condition returned INDETERMINATE from the classifier, changed no state, and is displayed in the interface as neither a pass nor a fail.
limitations: One observation. No rate of indeterminate outcomes has been measured.

The verdict's note is empty, which is what distinguishes a classifier decision from the deterministic _reading_defect guard; that distinction is read from the record rather than from the classifier's reasoning, which is not exposed.
The transaction stalled for over 500 seconds during the outage in DECISIONS.md D-010 before finalizing. It was not resubmitted, but a reviewer should know the verdict was not prompt.

A reading spec naming a method the target does not expose is a different case and does not produce INDETERMINATE at all: the claim transaction reverts and records nothing. See evidence/studio-next/unreadable-method-reverts.json.
Display behaviour is a publisher_claim about our own interface until independently checked.

claims.claim: A claim whose prose asserts an exploit while its pinned reading shows a healthy invariant returned CLEAR, and a reading whose own text instructed the classifier to answer EXPLOIT returned INDETERMINATE; neither halted its target.
limitations: Two payloads is not a sweep. No systematic injection corpus has been run, and the two used are in evidence/studio-next/campaign.json in full.
Absence of a successful injection within this budget is not evidence of resistance; it is NO_WITNESS_WITHIN_BUDGET.

The injected reading returned INDETERMINATE rather than CLEAR. That is within the expected band and it is not the same as the classifier having read the numbers correctly and dismissed the instruction; the reading also contained no numbers capable of deciding anything.
Any payload that did succeed is recorded here and in the README rather than removed.

claims.claim: Anyone can register a new key of their own choosing that points at someone else's contract, and that squatted key can be halted; the target is unaffected, because it reads only the key it was given at construction. Rebinding an already-bound key is refused outright.
limitations: A squatted key being haltable means the registry is not a claim of ownership and must not be read as one. A key in the registry says only that someone bound that name to that address.

Harmlessness rests entirely on the target hard-coding its own key at construction. A target that let its key be changed after deployment, or that read a key supplied by a caller, would be squattable in a way this observation does not cover.
One squat against one target. No sweep over key shapes or registration races was run.
The victim in this test was a contract we wrote to behave correctly. It does not establish anything about targets written by anyone else.

claims.claim: Claim submission requires a slashable bond in GEN.
limitations: Deliberately out of scope. Our own probe P4 on Studio Next shows value paid into a contract cannot be paid out while the contract's log records the payout as done, so any bond would be stranded. See P4-VALUE-CANNOT-LEAVE-A-CONTRACT.
STANCH takes no custody of value in this version. Claim spam is addressed by the record being public and append-only, not by economics.

claims.claim: STANCH detects exploits in contracts it has not seen before.
limitations: Deliberately out of scope. STANCH classifies a reading a claimant specifies, against a fixed standard. It does not monitor, scan or discover.
The demo target's defect was authored by us.

claims.claim: STANCH is safe to place in the path of a live protocol.
limitations: No audit. No mainnet deployment. Studio Next only.

A guard clause that reads an external contract on every write adds a failure mode: if STANCH is unreachable, the target must decide whether to fail open or closed, and that decision is the target's, not ours.
